title: Boeing Stock in Focus as Qantas Nears 20-Jet Order
summary: Boeing stock is in focus after Bloomberg reported Qantas is close to picking Boeing for most of an order for about 20 long-range jets.
body_markdown:
At the time, Reuters said Qantas operated some 128 jets and was in the middle of a fleet renewal program involving 200 aircraft. It had outstanding orders for 12 Boeing 787s and 24 larger Airbus A350-1000s, including 12 of a new Ultra-Long Range variant designed for nonstop flights from Australia's east coast to London or New York under "Project Sunrise." Qantas also holds options to buy more jets, split evenly between Airbus and Boeing, and Reuters' sources said some of these could be exercised.


## Why Is Qantas Ordering New Long-Range Jets?


The order is part of Qantas' wider fleet renewal, which includes retiring its aging Airbus A380 aircraft and adding more fuel-efficient long-haul jets, according to the Bloomberg report carried by Investing.com. Rising fuel prices amid the conflict involving Iran have added urgency to that plan, Bloomberg reported.


Bloomberg also said Qantas is expanding its 787 Dreamliner operations. Qantas has been a regular battleground for the two planemakers: its choice of Boeing's composite 787 two decades ago partly forced Airbus to drop its original, less ambitious A350 design, Reuters noted in June.


## Xiamen Airlines Agrees to Buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 Jets


A Qantas deal would follow other recent wins. Bloomberg pointed to Boeing's largest order from a major Chinese airline in almost a decade and its first widebody aircraft deal from Malaysia Airlines since 1995, per Investing.com.


China Southern Airlines said its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines agreed on Tuesday (Nov. 24) to buy 50 Boeing 737 MAX 8 planes at a list price of about US$7.4 billion, according to[Reuters](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/business/international/2026/11/25/china-southern-orders-50-jets-in-boeings-biggest-china-deal-in-nearly-a-decade/) . Airlines typically receive a large discount on the list price, and the jets are scheduled for delivery in batches between 2031 and 2034, subject to approval from the company's shareholders and relevant Chinese government authorities.


Reuters said the order follows a commitment for 200 jets that China made during a summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing in May. Jefferies said in a research note that it understood the order represented the first conversion of that commitment into a firm order, though China Southern's securities filing did not say whether it was included. Boeing, whose shares rose 1% on Tuesday, declined to comment. The planemaker had been largely shut out of new orders from China since 2017 amid U.S.-China trade tensions, Reuters reported.


The table below sums up the order news in this story, based on the Bloomberg report carried by Investing.com and Reuters coverage.
